name: ChatGPT
line: ChatGPT answers what a learner asks, in a chat. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs ChatGPT: ChatGPT answers what a learner asks, in a chat. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: ChatGPT answers what a learner asks, in a conversation, and its study mode guides with questions, hints and quizzes inside that chat [1]. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous. Every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. In ChatGPT the learner or the adult decides what to ask next [1]. Study mode gauges a learner's level from questions and memory of earlier chats, inside the conversation [1].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything hangs off the problem: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In ChatGPT the unit is the conversation. A learner brings a question, and study mode answers with guiding questions, hints and quizzes in the chat [1].

reasons.title: A hint never gives the answer
reasons.body: AMP's hint gives the first step and never the answer. An answer given after a hint or a lesson is marked as helped and does not count as learned. A skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once. Study mode aims to guide instead of answer, and OpenAI lists turning it on and off during a conversation as a feature [1]. A parent with a linked teen account can turn it on from parental controls, and OpenAI's page does not say it can be locked on [3]. In a field experiment with nearly 1,000 high school math students in Turkey, unrestricted GPT-4 raised practice scores by 48%, and once access was removed those students scored 17% lower on exams than students who never had AI. A tutor version with learning safeguards largely mitigated that harm [7].

reasons.title: Every answer checked exactly
reasons.body: After every answer AMP shows whether it was right, the correct answer and the worked steps. No AI model runs while a learner works: every problem, hint and explanation comes from tested code, and answers are checked exactly. OpenAI's terms warn that ChatGPT's output may not always be accurate [2], and OpenAI says study mode may make mistakes across conversations [1].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. In ChatGPT, study mode quizzes a learner inside a chat and can draw on memory of earlier chats [1]. We found no rule for when a skill is learned and no review schedule in OpenAI's description of study mode [1]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [11].

rows.range: No set range. The learner brings the topic, and study mode's examples include Bayes' theorem and game theory [1].
rows.start: No separate test. Study mode gauges level with questions and memory of earlier chats, inside the conversation [1].
rows.teaching: Answers in a chat. Study mode guides with questions, hints and quizzes instead of only giving the answer [1].
rows.next: Whatever the learner or the adult asks next [1].
rows.mastery: None found in the pages we read [1].
rows.review: Quizzes inside a chat, and memory of earlier chats. No review schedule found in OpenAI's description [1].
rows.adult: Chooses the topics and their order, judges what is learned and plans review [1]. Can turn study mode on from parental controls [3].
rows.reports: The chat history. Parental controls cover quiet hours, memory, voice and alerts on signs of acute distress, not learning [3].
rows.evidence: No outcome study of study mode found [1]. In a trial, students who practiced with unrestricted GPT-4 scored 17% lower on later exams than students without AI [7].

theirs: ChatGPT is a general AI chatbot from OpenAI. It is not sold as a math curriculum. A learner asks about a problem, and ChatGPT explains in the chat. This page is about using it as a learner's math tutor.

In study mode, ChatGPT works through problems step by step with guiding questions, hints and quizzes, instead of only giving an answer, and it gauges a learner's level from questions and memory of earlier chats [1]. The learner or the adult decides what to ask, in what order, and when to move on [1]. Google's Guided Learning for Gemini and the learning mode in Anthropic's Claude for Education also guide with questions instead of giving answers [4][5].
credit: Study mode was written with teachers, scientists and experts in teaching, around guiding questions, hints and checks for understanding [1].
It answers the learner's own question, from any book, and explains it again in other words when the first try does not land.

theirs: We found no study of ChatGPT's study mode that measures K-12 math outcomes. OpenAI writes that research on AI in education is still taking shape and that longer studies will follow [1]. Google's Guided Learning announcement reports no outcome data [4], and the LearnLM technical report evaluates the model family behind it by expert raters' preferences, not by what students learned [6]. We found no entry for general-purpose AI chatbots in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [9][10].

The most direct test of a chatbot as a math helper is a field experiment by Bastani and colleagues, published in PNAS in 2025 [7]. Classes of nearly 1,000 students in grades 9 to 11 at a high school in Turkey were randomly assigned to plain GPT-4, a GPT-4 tutor given teacher-written solutions and told to hint without revealing answers, or no AI, over four 90-minute sessions. Plain GPT-4 raised practice scores by 48% and lowered later exam scores, taken without AI, by 17% against the no-AI group. The tutor version largely mitigated that harm. Its exam scores were statistically indistinguishable from the control group's [7].

Khanmigo is Khan Academy's AI tutor, a different product. In a two-year randomized trial in 18 Tennessee middle schools, adding Khan Academy with Khanmigo to daily math intervention sessions raised scores by about 0.06 to 0.08 standard deviations a year, gains the authors say resemble what Khan Academy practice without AI predicts. The median student messaged Khanmigo in only 17% of the exercise sessions in which they made a mistake [8]. It is a working paper, not yet peer reviewed.
ours: The two findings that bear most on this comparison: across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, feedback that explains had the largest average effect, 0.49, against 0.32 for the correct answer alone and 0.05 for right or wrong only [12]; and mixed, spaced practice scored 62% against 38% for practice in blocks a month later, in a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations [11]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: Your child is stuck on one problem from another program and wants it explained another way.
amp: You want the program to place your child and choose each next problem.
You want every answer checked exactly, with the worked steps after it.
You want a hint that gives the first step and never the answer.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
You want to see a level for each part of math and the actual problems behind it.

questions.question: How is AMP different from ChatGPT?
questions.answer: ChatGPT answers what a learner asks in a chat, and study mode guides with questions, hints and quizzes [1]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, answers are checked exactly, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does ChatGPT work?
questions.answer: We found no study of study mode's effect on math learning, and OpenAI says longer studies will follow [1]. In a randomized field experiment, high school students with unrestricted GPT-4 scored 17% lower on later exams than students without it, and a tutor version with safeguards largely mitigated that harm [7].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. A learner can practice in AMP and ask a chatbot to explain an idea another way. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
